title: Preserve legacy RSA interoperability with explicit padding
goal: Replace obsolete Boolean RSACryptoServiceProvider calls with explicit legacy padding when preserving a peer ciphertext contract and existing Windows CAPI key access.

selectionNotes: Replace obsolete Boolean RSACryptoServiceProvider calls with explicit legacy padding when preserving a peer ciphertext contract and existing Windows CAPI key access.

providers: Windows CAPI RSACryptoServiceProvider; measured Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider type24, ephemeral RSA2048
platforms: Windows x64 CoreCLR; real CAPI operations required. Other providers/platforms and production containers not verified.
prerequisites: Workload-free net11.0 console project, C#15 sample mode, Nullable and ImplicitUsings enabled.
An existing agreed Boolean fOAEP contract and access to the same CAPI key; disposable ephemeral RSA2048 test key for verification.
constraints: true maps to OaepSHA1; false maps to Pkcs1. Compatibility only, neither is a new-protocol recommendation.
Same CAPI provider rejects OAEP-SHA256. Stronger-provider/algorithm/key migration requires separate peer agreement and positive proof, outside this slice.
No fallback after decrypt failure; production key containers/HSMs and authenticated-encryption redesign are outside this guide.

Framework APIs only; no NuGet packages, workloads, rendering mode or experimental opt-ins. Previous SDK10.0.402/runtime10.0.13 and current SDK11RC2/runtime11RC2 are verification pins, not supported consumer minimums.
stabilityLimitations: Stable APIs; actual .NET11 GA reconciliation remains open. RC2 evidence is not final-GA proof.

sources.title: Boolean padding diagnostic and compatibility mappings
Windows CAPI padding implementation and limits

evidence.scope: Windows paired compile/run with real ephemeral CAPI RSA2048: both legacy mappings cross-decrypt between runtimes in both directions; explicit overload equivalence, wrong padding/zeroed ciphertext and OAEP-SHA256 failure. Current old-source SYSLIB0064 probe and warning-free supported consumer; no other-platform/GA claim.
